subject.title: Feature: Auto session split when approaching context window limit

question: Should OpenClaw add token-pressure-based automatic session rollover, and should it be a standalone context-rollover policy or part of a broader session lifecycle/TTL design?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the requested behavior defines public config and changes session routing, continuity, memory, and delivery semantics across long-running sessions.

options.title: Design one opt-in lifecycle policy
options.body: Define token-pressure rollover, durable handoff, delivery identity preservation, config, docs, and tests in one maintainer-approved core session lifecycle design.

options.title: Fold into TTL rotation work
options.body: Keep this as a requirement of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/45390 so age, turn, and token-pressure rotation share one policy surface.

options.title: Defer automatic rollover
options.body: Keep compaction and manual/time-based reset as the supported mitigations while documenting operator-managed rotation for long-running deployments.

recommendation.title: Design one opt-in lifecycle policy
recommendation.body: Define token-pressure rollover, durable handoff, delivery identity preservation, config, docs, and tests in one maintainer-approved core session lifecycle design.

likelyOwner.reason: The central session/reset and memory-flush history points to steipete as the best available owner for the cross-boundary lifecycle decision.
